title: Connector status, credentials tests, requirements
request: Every data source on Home and in the wizard must work for real (the owner chose unstructured files, Kaggle and Hugging Face, databases and cloud, and synthetic data), including when credentials must stay on the server side; each source becomes a file in the draft and goes through the same structure, clean and analyse pipeline as an upload. This package says which sources are configured without revealing any secret, and makes a fresh environment able to read every format.
spec: GET /api/connectors (what is configured, by name only), tests that no secret leaks, and the libraries in requirements/base.txt. Done when tests/test_connectors.py passes and requirements/base.txt lists pyarrow, openpyxl, huggingface-hub, SQLAlchemy, boto3 and google-cloud-storage.
plan: Add connectors.status() and GET /api/connectors: configured sources and missing libraries, names and booleans only.
Import each connector library lazily so the product starts without it and the page names the missing one.
Test that keys, tokens and connection strings never appear in drafts, events, responses or error messages.

decisions.decision: Each library is imported only when its source is used.
decisions.why: The product still starts on a machine without the optional drivers, and the page says what to install.

decisions.decision: A refused credential never echoes the key.
decisions.why: Error messages are shown to users and written to logs.

change: connectors.status() and GET /api/connectors; secret-leak tests; requirements/base.txt lists the data-source libraries.

findings.defect: A fresh environment could not open an .xlsx upload or keep a cleaned table.
findings.scenario: Home and the wizard read Parquet, Excel, Hugging Face datasets, databases and cloud objects, but none of those libraries were in the requirements file; on this machine openpyxl was missing, so an Excel import downloaded and then failed when the pipeline read it.
findings.cause: Optional imports were never written down.
findings.fix: List the libraries in requirements/base.txt; install openpyxl here with the owner's approval.
findings.test: tests/test_connectors.py checks status() names the missing package.

outcome: Done: the status route names configured sources without secrets, no secret appears anywhere in tests, and the requirements list the libraries.
lessons: An optional dependency that the product needs for a promised feature belongs in the requirements, even if it is imported lazily.
